summary:
Windows 11 25H2 Settings, page by page, for the places where gnome-control-center 50.3 functions will land. This is from memory, not checked on a running Windows machine. Each item gives the Windows control in order with EN and NL wording, and in 'backing' the exact GNOME counterpart, checked against the files installed here: the schemas in /usr/share/glib-2.0/schemas with Ubuntu overrides, the polkit actions in /usr/share/polkit-1/actions, the D-Bus interfaces and service files, and the GTK UI strings built into /usr/bin/gnome-control-center. 'Windows-only (omit)' means GNOME has no such function. 'WinPoint shell' means WinPoint must keep the setting itself (settings.get/set).

English wording: en-GB, because WinPoint already uses Personalisation, Colours and Flight mode; en-US is noted where it differs. Dutch strings marked '(nl unverified)' should be checked on a real nl-NL 25H2 machine before they are frozen in kit::t.

Mouse, the example Robin gave: the Windows page is Primary mouse button, Mouse pointer speed, Enhance pointer precision, the Scrolling section and two Related settings links. All core rows map 1:1 to org.gnome.desktop.peripherals.mouse:
- Primary mouse button → left-handed
- Pointer speed (1–20) → speed, (n−10)/10
- Enhance pointer precision → accel-profile, default or flat
- Scrolling direction → natural-scroll
Additional mouse settings should be a native GTK version of the classic 'Eigenschappen voor Muis' dialog. Its Double-click speed slider → double-click. 'Show location of pointer when I press Ctrl' → locate-pointer. Scheme → cursor-theme. The dialog is also the place for GNOME's middle-click emulation and Test Settings.

GNOME functions that Windows has nowhere, and the Windows-style home proposed for each:
- Wellbeing (screen time, daily limit, greyscale, break reminders): extra section on System › Focus.
- Workspaces dynamic/fixed/number, workspaces only on primary, hot corner: Multitasking › Desktops.
- Over-amplification: Accessibility › Audio.
- Visual alerts: Audio, 'Flash my screen'.
- Activate windows on hover, simulated secondary click, hover click: Accessibility › Mouse.
- Crosshairs and colour effects: Magnifier.
- Status shapes: Visual effects.
- Cursor blinking: Text cursor.
- Compose and AltGr key, keyboard shortcuts editor, repeat delay/rate: Advanced keyboard settings, plus a native 'Keyboard Properties' dialog.
- Week numbers, weekday, world clocks: Date & time.
- Login-screen language/formats/keyboard: Administrative language settings.
- Media sharing (rygel) and connectivity checking: Advanced network settings.
- Thunderbolt: Bluetooth & devices › USB.
- Device security (fwupd HSI) and Ubuntu Security Center: Privacy & security › Windows Security.
- Ubuntu error/system reporting: Diagnostics & feedback.
- Search providers: Search permissions.
- Search locations: Searching Windows.
- Trash and temp auto-delete: System › Storage › Storage Sense.
- Restore windows after login: Sign-in options.
- Automatic login, fingerprint, password: Sign-in options.
- Privacy screen, Adjust for TV, legacy-app scaling: Display.
- Remote Login (headless) and Secure Shell: Remote Desktop and System › Advanced.
- WWAN: a Mobile page.
- Wacom: Pen & Windows Ink.
- Removable-media types: AutoPlay.
- Online accounts: Email & accounts.
- Per-app portal permissions: Apps › Advanced options.

Things that are absent on this install and should be hidden: gnome-user-share (File Sharing, password-protected sharing), openssh-server (offer an install through PackageKit instead), malcontent (Family / Parental Controls), usbguard (Forbid new USB devices). The per-monitor app-switcher key that g-c-c's strings mention is also missing from the installed org.gnome.shell schema.

Some keys are risky or unclear:
- Lid-close behaviour is mostly logind's job (root config); the gsd lid-close-* keys need checking before they are wired.
- Writing GNOME proxy credentials stores them in plain text in dconf.
- Colour filters have no GNOME 50 key at all.
- Windows splits several things that GNOME keeps as one value: screen-off timeout per power source (GNOME has one idle-delay), power-button action, and the Custom mode split between Windows mode and app mode.

System writes go through polkit, exactly as GNOME does (ids listed per item):
- hostname1, timedate1 and locale1
- AccountsService and fprintd
- NetworkManager, CupsPkHelper, colord and bolt
- UPower charge limit and power-profiles
- the gnome-remote-desktop system daemon
- WhoopsiePreferences, PackageKit, and the Ubuntu LanguageSelector D-Bus service

Some GNOME helpers are Python or GTK3 and must not run inside WinPoint: gnome-language-selector and check-language-support, and Orca's preferences dialog. Talk to their D-Bus backends instead, or write the schema keys natively.

I read the existing WinPoint host methods; matching ones are named in backing (system.brightness, system.nightLight, system.audio, system.network, system.bluetooth, display.set, apps.setDefault, index.*, storage.cleanup.*, clipboard.*, sysmon.*). No files were changed and nothing was run against the live session.
